note: No entries: the match is to be played, no set is open, and side 1 is due to serve (§ 1.2, § 10.4).
Four straight points win a game (ITF Rule 5); the receiver serves the next game (Rule 9).
From deuce a game needs two consecutive points: at advantage there is no game yet (Rule 5).
No-advantage scoring: at deuce the next point wins the game (Appendix VI).
At six games all a tie-break, first to seven by two, decides the set 7-6 (Rule 5(b), Rule 6).
Two sets of six love win a best-of-three match (Rule 7); a point after completion is ignored, not refused (§ 2.1, ignored 2).
A point that names no winner is ignored (§ 2.1, ignored 1); one that names a side 3 is refused (§ 2.1).
A side may be named 0-based (`winner`) or 1-based (`winningSide`); both name the same side (§ 1.3).
Whole games entered by `game` build a set as points do: six games to four wins it (§ 2.2, Rule 6).
Set totals entered by `set` close each set and decide the match (§ 2.3, § 9).
A late-start baseline sets the score before play (§ 2.5); points then play on from it: 5-4 and a love game make 6-4.
A `setServer` before the first point names side 2 to serve; the receiver of each game serves the next (§ 2.6, § 10.6).
A tiebreak-only set (`S:TB10`) is a race to ten points, two clear (§ 5).
A timed segment scored in points (`S:T10P`) plays until the host ends it (§ 6.4); `endSegment` closes it with the side ahead winning it.
`endSegment` ends timed segments only: on a standard set it is refused and changes nothing (§ 2.4).
A format that does not parse refuses every action that scores or names a server, and records the rest (§ 1.1, § 2): an annotation is kept. No server is reported.
An entry of a type the reducer does not know is kept in place and not replayed (§ 12.1).
A `challenge` names side 1 or 2 and changes no score; side 3 is refused (§ 2.8).
A consecutive-points game (`G:3C`) is won by the first side to win three points in a row (§ 4.1 rule 4).
At a set all, a final match tie-break (`F:TB10`) decides the match, first to ten by two (Appendix VI).
Where points are units (a timed segment in points) a point carries its `scoreValue`, and a multiplier gives one to a point by its result (§ 5 rule 5).

Under the competition's winner-serves rule the side that won the last point serves the next, even inside a game of a standard set, where service would otherwise stay with one side for the game (§ 10.7).
